title: openai /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability, function/tool-calls, roles/stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Ava Patel
description:
Motivation: Bring Redwood's OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat.completions behavior to parity for a set of fields that customers depend on: streaming stability for chunked responses, deterministic handling of roles and stop tokens, passthrough of stop/logprobs fields, and consistent response formatting (including structured output / function-calls compatibility). This PR implements the runtime and API-layer changes to match observed OpenAI semantics so downstream SDKs and integrations behave the same as they would against OpenAI endpoints. Changes include: 1) stabilize streaming protocol by flushing partial tokens only after queue ordering guarantees and backpressure fixes; 2) add function/tool-calling glue that maps OpenAI function call metadata into Redwood tool invocation hooks and back into streaming responses; 3) ensure roles are normalized (assistant/system/user) and message-attribution preserved across rollouts; 4) passthrough stop and logprobs where requested by client and expose consistent ordering in the delta stream; 5) improve response formatting so structured outputs (JSON schema / function return) have deterministic chunking and finalization. Checklist:
- [x] implement streaming ordering & backpressure fixes
- [x] add OpenAI-compatible function/tool-call handling and fallback routing
- [x] support stop/logprobs passthrough in both sync and streaming modes
- [x] normalize roles and add test coverage for edge cases (multi-stop tokens, nested function calls)
- [x] update Python/TS SDK compatibility layer and docs
- [x] manual QA on Dedicated cluster (small traffic)
Notes: Backwards-compatible by default; some behavior exposed behind feature flag "openai_chat_parity" for gradual rollout. Related linear items: ENG-5123 (streaming reliability), ENG-5240 (tool-calling parity), PM-210 (product compatibility).
commits: feat(api): add openai chat.completions parity shim and feature flag
fix(streaming): ordering/backpressure fix in streaming runtime (ensure chunk commit ordering)
feat(tooling): map OpenAI function_call metadata to Redwood tool-calling hooks
test: add integration coverage for roles/stop/logprobs in sync and streaming
docs: openai_compat.md updates and SDK example for function calls
perf: reduce allocations in streaming path; add microbench harness
ci_checks: integration-tests: flaky (streaming test failed first run, rerun passed)
review_comments: Liam Chen (2026-01-20): Left a couple of inline comments on streaming.py about ordering guarantees. Can we add a deterministic test that simulates concurrent chunk interleaving?

Ava Patel (2026-01-21): Added tests/unit/test_streaming_ordering.py to simulate interleaving and added a lock-free sequence check. Reply: test included and added a microbench to assert no perf regression.
María Gómez (2026-01-25): For function calls, how do we surface tool errors back to the OpenAI-compatible response? Recommend adding a structured error field in the delta stream.

Ava Patel (2026-01-25): Added mapping: tool errors are marshalled into a function_call.error field in the final event and we expose a structured hint in the response metadata. This behavior is behind the feature flag.
Ethan Brooks (2026-01-28): Verified role normalization; flagged one edge case where system messages with multi-line content lost trailing newline. Fixed in a small follow-up commit.
release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions parity: streaming stability improvements, function/tool-calling compatibility, roles normalization, stop/logprobs passthrough, and deterministic response formatting. Opt-in via feature flag 'openai_chat_parity' for staged rollout. Includes SDK updates and docs.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover ordering, role normalization, stop token and logprobs passthrough. Integration tests run against a Dedicated cluster with small traffic; ran synthetic concurrency test for streaming churn. Observability added: openai_parity_stream_latency and parity_stream_reorders metrics. One flaky streaming test failed on first CI run due to timing; rerun passed after adding a deterministic sequencing assertion.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag deployed off by default. Recommended rollout: enable for 5% of traffic in staging, monitor parity_stream_reorders and unit cost per token. Have rollback plan to disable feature flag and fallback to previous streaming implementation. Notify SRE channel before enabling on Dedicated clusters.
